dependent_species: Melitta nigricans – Purple loosestrife silk bee
description: Oligolectic bee on Lythrum; in Vienna along slow waters, reed margins and ditches (Lobau, Old Danube), local; thrives in large pots kept moist.

dependent_species: Macropis europaea – Yellow loosestrife oil bee
description: Oil‑collecting bee strictly bound to Lysimachia; in Vienna along canals, wet meadows and fen edges of the Donau‑Auen; grows well in tubs with constant moisture.

plant: Lotus corniculatus – Bird’s‑foot trefoil (balcony window box)

Larvae feed on clovers and grasses; in Vienna on poor meadows and fallows; declines with frequent mowing—retain late cuts in city greenspaces.
Larvae use vetches/peas; in Vienna along species‑rich margins and embankments (railway, Danube levees), fragmented populations.

plant: Rhamnus cathartica – Common buckthorn (compact hedge forms)
description: Larvae on buckthorn/blackthorn; in Vienna on warm, sunny hedgerows and scrubby edges (vineyard fringes), fragmented; dwarf hedging cultivars fit small gardens.

plant: Viola tricolor – Wild pansy (top balcony plant)
description: Larvae on violets; in Vienna on sandy poor grasslands and dry urban banks with Viola; thrives in planters and window boxes, flowers for months.
Provides nectar and low, open structure; skippers need flower‑rich edges in Vienna. Excellent for containers and balcony troughs; fruits for people and wildlife.
